pros: Emails sent from Gmail or Outlook log to the contact record automatically
Sequences unenrol prospects on reply and support task and call steps
Meeting links handle round robin assignment for shared inbound demos
Custom report builder joins contact, company, deal and activity data
Free CRM tier lets a two person team start without a consultant
cons: Sequences and custom reporting require the pricier Professional tier
Professional tier carries a mandatory onboarding fee on top of seats
No built in third party contact data, so prospecting needs another provider
Complex multi-object models and territory rules are awkward next to Salesforce
verdict_line: Pick HubSpot Sales Hub if you want CRM, email, meetings and sequences from one vendor that reps will actually keep current.

pros: Contact database and sequencer in one seat costs less than buying both
Filters by title, headcount, tech stack, funding and recent hires
Saved searches surface new matching contacts as the database updates
Sequences include A/B steps, reply detection and mailbox rotation
Built in inbox warm-up and domain health checks help deliverability
cons: Coverage is thinner outside US technology and services companies
Mobile numbers are unreliable, so many teams verify with a second source
Deal tracking is too thin to replace a real CRM
Generic Apollo templates are widely recognised and underperform
verdict_line: Pick Apollo if you need contact data and sequencing in one affordable seat to launch a first outbound motion.

pros: Waterfall enrichment cascades through providers and only charges on a hit
Claygent research columns turn website reads into structured fields
One table can find, enrich, personalise and push to a sequencer
Tables run on a schedule so new signals route without manual work
Public template library covers most common outbound plays
cons: Needs a dedicated owner who thinks in tables and logic
Credit spend is hard to predict until a table has run
No sequencer, dialer or inbox, so a CRM and sender are still required
verdict_line: Pick Clay if a RevOps builder on your team wants to chain many data providers and AI research into custom list workflows.

pros: Search thousands of calls for a competitor name or objection phrase
Deal boards flag stalled deals and missing decision makers from call data
Curated call libraries and scorecards shorten new rep ramp
Writes captured contacts and activity back to Salesforce and HubSpot
AI account summaries let leaders prepare without reading full threads
cons: Per seat pricing plus platform fee is hard to justify under twenty reps
Value depends on managers actually reviewing calls each week
Recording consent needs legal review in Europe and regulated industries
Engagement tools lag dedicated sequencers like Apollo or Outreach
verdict_line: Pick Gong if you have twenty plus reps and managers who will coach from recorded calls every week.
